summary: Backend-only verification of the startup-cron init guard + admin alerting (safeInitCron / buildCronInitAlert / shouldAlertCronInit / _alertCronInitFailure in js/_index.js). Created pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_cron_init_alert.py (7 tests, all PASS, run twice for flake check). POST /api/dev/cron-init-alert-test → 200, pass:true, exactly 12 checks all true; injected sink captured ONLY unit_bad (no real Telegram send), alertText has heading 'Startup cron failed to load' + cron name + error and HTML-escapes <, >, & (raw '<detail>' absent); dedup first=true/second=false; endpoint is idempotent across repeated calls (failuresIncrementedByOne uses a delta). Boot resilience: restarted supervisor 'nodejs', post-restart log block shows '[HostingUpgradeNudge] Initialized', '[ProtectionEnforcer] Initialized and scheduled', '[ProtectionHeartbeat] Initialized and scheduled' and (after ~60s) '[BifurcationHealCron] Scheduled — daily at 03:30 UTC'; the only '[CronInit] ❌' lines in the log are 'unit_bad' from the dev test calls — no real startup-cron failures and no 'Cannot find module' from boot. Regression: /api/dev/admin-media-confirm-test, /api/dev/escalation-alert-plan-test, /api/dev/promo-cadence-test, /api/dev/admin-media-reply-test all pass:true; /api/health healthy + database connected. Safety honoured: no Telegram webhook driving, no /admin/* calls.
critical_code_review_comments: Optional hardening: _cronInitFailures is only visible in-process; consider exposing it (count + names) on /api/health or an admin diagnostic so a failed startup cron is also detectable without relying on the Telegram DM landing.
_cronInitAlerted dedup is per-process, so every pod restart re-alerts the same broken cron. Acceptable (loud is the goal) but worth a note if restart churn could spam the admin chat.

_alertCronInitFailure fires in dev pods too (TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID is set); unlike escalationReminderTick it has no BOT_ENVIRONMENT/SKIP_WEBHOOK_SYNC dev guard, so a dev-only module break would DM the production admin. Consider gating or prefixing the alert with the environment.
seed_data_creation: None — dev endpoint is pure/in-memory with an injected alert sink; no Mongo writes.
test_credentials: No auth needed; /api/dev/* enabled via BOT_ENVIRONMENT=development
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable suite: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_cron_init_alert.py (uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env). Note that each run of /api/dev/cron-init-alert-test intentionally logs one "[CronInit] ❌ 'unit_bad' ... Cannot find module '/x/y'" line — ignore those when auditing boot logs. Startup-cron log markers appear ~145-150 lines after the '🚀 Early health check server started on port 5000' boot marker; BifurcationHealCron schedules ~60s after restart, so wait before asserting.
rca_of_the_issue: Original regression: BifurcationHealCron require() threw and was swallowed by an info-level try/catch, so the daily sweep silently never scheduled. Fix verified: safeInitCron logs with a ❌ marker, records the failure, and Telegrams the admin (once per name), while never throwing so boot continues; previously unguarded inits (ProtectionEnforcer, ProtectionHeartbeat, HostingUpgradeNudge) are now wrapped and the existing catches for cPanelHealth, WhmDiskMonitor, CallBillingReconciler, RateDeckSync, BifurcationHealCron now alert.
